newsitem.title: USA: Eastern U.S. corn belt freeze could nip corn, soy.
newsitem.headline: Eastern U.S. corn belt freeze could nip corn, soy.

text.p: Freezing temperatures forecast for the Midwest Thursday night could damage late-planted soybean and corn crops, but agronomists said most areas would escape serious damage.
"The majority of it (corn and soybean crop) is not going to be affected," said Mike Clark, extension agent with the Illinois Agricultural Statistics Service.

Weather Services Corp forecast a freeze line as far south as Peoria, Ill. and extending eastward to Dayton, Ohio Thursday night. Temperatures were seen dipping into the 30s F, but could fall further if cloud cover clears, they said.
"The majority of our corn is on the verge of putting down its black layer, but we could lose some," said Tim Barney, agronomist with the The Andersons Inc in Fulton, Ohio.
Corn in the black layer stage has finished growing and is less susceptible to damage from freezing temperatures.
Barney said that soybeans in his area would be vulnerable, but growing conditions were so variable that plant damage would be isolated.
The Illinois soybean crop was viewed as more likely to sustain damage from frost than the corn crop because it was planted much later than corn in most areas, Clark said.
Illinois' corn crop was 83 percent mature as of Sunday, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said. Seventy-three percent of soybeans were dropping leaves as of Sunday.
In Ohio, 40 percent of the corn crop was rated mature as of Sunday and 76 percent of the soybean crop was dropping leaves, according to the latest crop progress report.
